Jesus: Accounts of Jesus's life are contained in the Gospels, especially the four canonical Gospels of the New Testament.
In what year was Angela Merkel born?
Angela Merkel: Angela Dorothea Merkel (née Kasner; born 17 July 1954) is a German stateswoman and retired politician who served as Chancellor of Germany from 2005 to 2021.
In what year was Gerald Ford born?
Gerald Ford: Gerald Rudolph Ford Jr. (born Leslie Lynch King Jr.; July 14, 1913 – December 26, 2006) was the 38th president of the United States, serving from 1974 to 1977.
In what year did Madame du Barry die?
Madame du Barry: Jeanne Bécu, Comtesse du Barry (French: [baʁi]; 19 August 1743 – 8 December 1793) was the last maîtresse-en-titre of King Louis XV of France.
In what year did Cleopatra die?
Cleopatra: Born in Alexandria, Cleopatra was the daughter of Ptolemy XII Auletes, who named her his heir before his death in 51 BC.
In what year was Rashidun Caliphate founded?
Rashidun Caliphate: The title Rashidun stems from the doctrine in Sunni Islam that the caliphs were "rightly guided".
In what year was Renaissance (French political party) founded?
Renaissance (RE) is a political party in France that is typically described as liberal and centrist or centre-right.

Russian Empire: Peter the Great. It also colonized Alaska between 1799 and 1867.
National Action Party (Mexico): Manuel Gómez Morín. The National Action Party (Spanish: Partido Acción Nacional, PAN) is a conservative political party in Mexico founded in 1939.
In which country was Whigs (British political party) based?
Whigs (British political party): United Kingdom. The Whigs were a political party in the Parliaments of England, Scotland, Ireland, Great Britain and the United Kingdom.
Which country is Bolshoi Theatre from?
Bolshoi Theatre: Russia. The Bolshoi Ballet and Bolshoi Opera are among the oldest and best known ballet and opera companies in the world.
In which country is Sinking of MV Sewol?
Sinking of MV Sewol: South Korea. On the morning of Wednesday, 16 April 2014, the ferry MV Sewol sank while en route from Incheon towards Jeju City in South Korea.
In which country is Black Lives Matter?
Black Lives Matter: United States. Its primary concerns are police brutality and racially motivated violence against Black people.
In which country did the Battle of Sirte (2011) take place?
Battle of Sirte (2011): Libya. The battle and its aftermath marked the fall of the final stronghold of Gaddafi loyalists.
In which country is Battle of Monte Cassino?
Battle of Monte Cassino: Italy. The objective was to break through the Winter Line and facilitate an advance towards Rome.
In which country is Kent State shootings?
Kent State shootings: United States. The shootings triggered immediate and massive outrage on campuses around the country.
In which country is British royal family?
British royal family: United Kingdom. The British royal family comprises King Charles III and other members of his family.
In which country was the Sultanate of Mogadishu?
Sultanate of Mogadishu: Somalia. Established by Abubakr bin Fakhr ad-Din, who served as the first Sultan of the Mogadishu Sultanate and the Fakhr al-Din dynasty.
Which of these was an official language of Independent State of Croatia?
Independent State of Croatia: Croatian. The Independent State of Croatia (Croatian: Nezavisna Država Hrvatska, NDH) was a World War II–era quasi-state.
Which of these was an official language of the Roman Empire?
Roman Empire: Latin. The Roman Empire was a state that dominated the Mediterranean and much of Europe, Western Asia, and North Africa during the classical period.
Which of these was an official language of July Monarchy?
July Monarchy: French. It marks the end of the Bourbon Restoration (1814–1830).
Of which country is Old Catalan an official language?
Old Catalan is an official language of Crown of Aragon. The larger Crown of Aragon must not be confused with one of its constituent parts, the Kingdom of Aragon, from which it takes its name.
In Greek mythology, this king of Mycenae commanded the Achaean forces during the Trojan War and was killed by his wife Clytemnestra upon his return home. Who is he?
Agamemnon (Ancient) was a king of Mycenae who commanded the Achaeans during the Trojan War.

This early-20th-century Indian rebel leader took up ascetic renunciation at 18 and added a name in memory of a lost love, before leading a famous jungle uprising against British colonizers — who is he?
Alluri Sitarama Raju (4 July 1897 or 1898 - 7 May 1924) was an Indian revolutionary who waged an armed rebellion against the British colonial rule in India.
Before serving as a government minister overseeing sport and broadcasting, this four-time member of India's parliament led the country's cricket governing body from 2015 to 2017 — who is he?
Anurag Thakur (born 24 October 1974) is an Indian politician from the Bharatiya Janata Party and a Member of Parliament in the Lok Sabha from Hamirpur, Himachal Pradesh.

Fought over two days in June 1314 between Robert the Bruce and England's Edward II, this decisive Scottish clash during the siege of a royal castle became a turning point in the fight for independence — which clash?

Battle of Bannockburn (Scottish) was fought on 23-24 June 1314, between the army of Robert the Bruce, King of Scots, and the army of King Edward II of England, during the First War of Scottish Independence.

Traditionally credited to an 8th-century BCE prophet but believed by modern scholars to blend the work of at least three authors across centuries, which text opens the major prophets of the Christian Old Testament?
Book of Isaiah is the first of the Latter Prophets in the Hebrew Bible and the first of the major prophets in the Christian Old Testament.
Flying the Spirit of St. Louis alone for over 33 hours to win the $25,000 Orteig Prize, this aviator completed the first solo nonstop transatlantic flight in May 1927 — who is he?
Charles Lindbergh (February 4, 1902 - August 26, 1974) was an American aviator, military officer, and author.

This Anatolian mother goddess, with a possible forerunner in Neolithic Çatalhöyük, had her Phrygian cult adopted by Greek colonists and spread across the Greek world by the sixth century BC — who is she?
Cybele is an Anatolian mother goddess; she may have a possible forerunner in the earliest Neolithic at atalhyk.
Nicknamed after a Renaissance artist, this Ukrainian soldier became the youngest battalion commander in his country's military history while leading a right-wing volunteer movement — who was he?
Dmytro Kotsiubailo (1 November 1995 - 7 March 2023) was a Ukrainian volunteer, soldier, lieutenant, a commander of the 1st Mechanized Battalion of the Armed Forces of Ukraine.
Convicted of war crimes at Nuremberg, this German grand admiral commanded the Kriegsmarine until 1943, when Karl Dönitz took over — who is he?
Erich Raeder (24 April 1876 - 6 November 1960) was a German admiral who played a major role in the naval history of World War II and was convicted of war crimes after the war.
The only Central African president born in modern-day Gabon, this former army chief led the country from 2003 to 2013 — who is he?
François Bozizé (born 14 October 1946) is a Central African politician who was President of the Central African Republic from 2003 to 2013.
The Philippines' longest-serving president since Marcos, she was also the country's first female vice president before taking the top office in 2001 — who is she?
Gloria Macapagal Arroyo (born April 5, 1947), often referred to as PGMA or GMA, is a Filipino academic and politician who served as the 14th president of the Philippines from 2001 to 2010.

Commissioned into a light horse unit his own father raised, he became the first Australian to reach lieutenant general and led the Desert Mounted Corps to one of military history's fastest pursuits. Who was this WWI commander?

Harry Chauvel (16 April 1865 - 4 March 1945) was a senior officer of the Australian Imperial Force who fought at Gallipoli and during the Sinai and Palestine Campaign in the Middle Eastern theatre of the First World War.

Founded in 2021 by former presidential candidate Muharrem İnce after splitting from the country's main opposition, this movement echoed the spirit of Atatürk in its slogan and dissolved itself in 2025 — what was it called?

Homeland Party (Turkey, 2021) was a political party in Turkey, founded in May 2021 by Muharrem nce, the former candidate of the Republican People's Party (CHP) in the 2018 Turkish presidential election.
This Spanish politician has served as president of the Community of Madrid since 2019, and also leads the regional branch of Spain's People's Party — who is she?
Isabel Díaz Ayuso (born 17 October 1978) is a Spanish politician who has served as the president of the Community of Madrid since 2019.

A Democratic attorney and Army National Guard officer who served in Kandahar Province, this North Carolina official became the state's 52nd attorney general in 2025 after previously representing its 14th congressional district — who is he?
Jeff Jackson (politician) (born September 12, 1982) is an American politician, attorney, and Army National Guard officer who has served as the 52nd attorney general of North Carolina since 2025.
When he finally stepped down in 2017, he was Africa's second-longest-serving president — the man who led Angola and its ruling MPLA for nearly four decades. Who is it?
José Eduardo dos Santos (Portuguese; 28 August 1942 - 8 July 2022) was an Angolan politician and military officer who served as the second president of Angola from 1979 to 2017.

Generally credited with commissioning the Great Pyramid of Giza, this Fourth Dynasty pharaoh who succeeded his father Sneferu survives in only one complete portrait — a tiny ivory figurine. Who is he?
Khufu was the second pharaoh of the Fourth Dynasty of Egypt, reigning during the 26th century BC in the early Old Kingdom period.
The first president of Ukraine, he led the country to independence from the Soviet Union and oversaw the handover of its nuclear arsenal before an economic crisis cost him re-election — who was he?
Leonid Kravchuk (10 January 1934 - 10 May 2022) was a Ukrainian politician who served as the first president of Ukraine from 5 December 1991 to 19 July 1994.
This economist-turned-politician became Moldova's first female president in 2020, after previously serving as prime minister for a few months in 2019 — who is she?
Maia Sandu (born 24 May 1972) is a Moldovan politician and economist who, since 2020, has served as the sixth president of Moldova.
This Royal Navy navigator led the first inshore circumnavigation of mainland Australia and championed the very name "Australia" as "more agreeable to the ear." Who was he?

Matthew Flinders (16 March 1774 - 19 July 1814) was an English Royal Navy officer, navigator and cartographer who led the first inshore circumnavigation of mainland Australia, then called New Holland.
Spending most of his career in Kuwait's security and intelligence services and once the world's oldest crown prince, this royal became Emir of Kuwait at age 83 in 2023 — who is he?
Mishal Al-Ahmad Al-Jaber Al-Sabah (born 27 September 1940) is Emir of Kuwait, reigning since 2023.
This ongoing rural conflict between India's government and communist guerrilla factions traces back to a 1967 village uprising that fractured the Communist Party of India — what is it known as?
Naxalite–Maoist insurgency is an ongoing conflict between the Government of India and left-wing extremist groups.

Flourishing in what is now Veracruz and Tabasco from roughly 1200 to 400 BC, this early Mesoamerican civilization relocated its center from San Lorenzo to La Venta after the former's decline — who were they?
Olmecs were an early major Mesoamerican civilization, flourishing in the modern-day Mexican states of Veracruz and Tabasco from roughly 1200 to 400 BC during Mesoamerica's formative period.
A Rhodes Scholar and Harvard graduate who once worked at McKinsey, this politician served as mayor of South Bend, Indiana, before becoming the 19th U.S. secretary of transportation — who is he?
Pete Buttigieg (born January 19, 1982) is an American politician and former naval officer who served as the 19th United States secretary of transportation from 2021 to 2025.
On this recurring April Fools' social experiment, registered users could color a single pixel on a shared online canvas, then had to wait minutes before placing another — what's the Reddit project?
R/place was a recurring collaborative project and social experiment hosted on the content aggregator site Reddit.
This explorer became the first person in history to walk to both the North and South Poles, and later founded an organization dedicated to preserving Antarctica — who is he?
Robert Swan (born 28 July 1956) is the first person to walk to both poles.

This Spanish politician has led the far-right party Vox since founding it in 2014, and now also presides over the pan-European Patriots.eu alliance, having earlier served in the Basque Parliament as a centre-right legislator. Who is he?
Santiago Abascal (born 14 April 1976) is a Spanish politician who has been the president of Vox, a far-right political party, since 2014.
Varieties of this political philosophy differ by how much they rely on markets versus planning, but all favor social ownership of production over private — which ideology is it?
Socialism is an economic and political philosophy encompassing diverse economic and social systems characterised by social ownership of the means of production, as opposed to private ownership.
Representing Massachusetts in the U.S. Senate from 1962 until his death in 2009, this Democratic lawmaker was the younger brother of a president and a U.S. attorney general — who was he?
Ted Kennedy (February 22, 1932 - August 25, 2009) was an American lawyer and politician who represented Massachusetts in the United States Senate from 1962 until his death in 2009.
Head of state for nearly 26 years and dominant in his nation's politics for 31, this Finnish president was so unopposed in later elections that historians often call him an autocrat — who was he?
Urho Kekkonen (3 September 1900 - 31 August 1986), often referred to by his initials UKK, was a Finnish politician who served as the eighth and longest-serving president of Finland from 1956 to 1982.
This actor turned investment strategist played Dr. Charley Michaels on House Calls from 1979 to 1982 — who is he?
Hieronymus Karl Friedrich, Freiherr von Münchhausen

A former prosecutor general who became the 13th president of South Korea in 2022, he served the shortest elected term in the country's democratic history before his removal — and is now serving a life sentence for heading an insurrection. Who is he?
Yoon Suk Yeol (born 18 December 1960) is a South Korean politician who served as the 13th president of South Korea from 2022 until his removal from office in 2025.
Blind in one eye from glaucoma and known affectionately as 'Gus Dur,' this Islamic scholar served as Indonesia's fourth president from 1999 until his removal in 2001 — who is he?
Abdurrahman Wahid: President of Indonesia from 1999 to 2001. On 17 January 2000, Abdurrahman issued Presidential Decree No. 6 of 2000 to annul the previous instruction.

Once the Chief Mufti of a breakaway Chechen republic, this politician switched allegiances during the Second Chechen War to become the region's president, before being assassinated by a bomb in Grozny in 2004. Who was he?
Akhmad Kadyrov: Chechen militant and revolutionary (1951–2004)
Editor of the Nazi Party's newspaper and head of its Office of Foreign Affairs throughout the regime, this Baltic German ideologue was later convicted as a war criminal — who was he?
Alfred Rosenberg: Nazi theorist and war criminal (1893–1946)
In Greek myth, this Trojan princess was Hector's grieving widow, later taken as a concubine by Neoptolemus after her young son was thrown from the city walls — who is she?
Andromache: Wife of Hector in Greek mythology.
Born in Dublin in 1769, this British officer-turned-twice-Prime-Minister defeated Tipu Sultan in the Anglo-Mysore wars before his Coalition crushed Napoleon at Waterloo — who was he?
Arthur Wellesley, 1st Duke of Wellington: British Army officer and statesman (1769–1852)
Hired by a Moabite king to curse the Israelites, this biblical prophet blessed them instead, as recounted in the Book of Numbers — who was he?
Balaam: Prophet in the Book of Numbers. Balaam is also mentioned in the Book of Micah, the Second Epistle of Peter, the Book of Jude, and the Book of Revelation.
The only British prime minister born Jewish, this Conservative statesman clashed repeatedly with Liberal rival William Gladstone — who is he?
Benjamin Disraeli: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom (1868; 1874–1880)
After Rome ignored her husband's will and annexed their kingdom, this queen of the Iceni tribe led a failed revolt against Roman rule in Britain around AD 60 — who was she?
Boudica: Queen of the British Iceni tribe (d. 60/61)
Crushed by the Albigensian Crusade and the Medieval Inquisition by 1350, this dualist Christian movement believed in two opposing gods — what was it called?
Catharism: Medieval southern European Christian dualist movement.

On 15 March 2019, a gunman attacked two New Zealand mosques during Friday prayer, killing 51 people in the first far-right terror attack to be successfully live-streamed on Facebook. What is this atrocity called?
Christchurch mosque shootings: 2019 terrorist attacks in New Zealand.

Possibly first captured as embers from lightning-struck blazes, this technology gave ancient hominins warmth, protection from predators, and a way to cook food, reshaping diet and migration — what is it?
Control of fire by early humans

Control of fire by early humans

Backed by President Nicolas Sarkozy, this French economist served as the IMF's tenth managing director from 2007 until resigning in 2011 amid scandal — who is he?
Dominique Strauss-Kahn: French economist and politician (born 1949)
This 21st-century movement uses evidence and reason to calculate which charities and careers do the most good, treating everyone's interests as equally weighty — what's it called?
Effective altruism: Philosophical and social movement.
This Turkish socialist academic-turned-politician leads the Workers' Party of Turkey and represents Istanbul in parliament — who is he?
A dependency-theory scholar before he was a head of state, this sociologist became the first Brazilian president to win re-election — who is he?
Fernando Henrique Cardoso: President of Brazil from 1995 to 2003.
Governing from 1946 to 1958, this parliamentary government presided over rapid postwar economic growth fueled by the Marshall Plan, despite chronic cabinet instability. What was it called?

French Fourth Republic: Government of France from 1946 to 1958. It also saw the beginning of the rapprochement with France's longtime enemy Germany, which led to Franco-German co-operation and eventually to the European Union.
This 43rd U.S. president served from 2001–2009. Born into a prominent political family, he was previously Texas governor and co-owned a baseball team. Who is he?
George W. Bush: President of the United States from 2001 to 2009.

Michigan's 49th governor, this Democrat gained national attention in 2013 for a state Senate floor speech in which she shared her own experience of sexual assault during an abortion debate. Who is she?
Gretchen Whitmer: Governor of Michigan since 2019.
Adam of Bremen called this King of Norway the "Thunderbolt of the North" — a man who spent 15 years in exile commanding the Byzantine Empire's Varangian Guard before his crown. Who was he?
Alfonso VI of León and Castile
Harald Hardrada: King of Norway from 1046 to 1066.

Rising through the Communist Youth League in Tibet, this Chinese politician later governed Hebei, led the Communist Party in Inner Mongolia and Guangdong, and served as Vice Premier from 2018 to 2023 — who is he?
Hu Chunhua: Vice Chairperson of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference since 2023.

Sparked by a failed operation to infiltrate forces into Kashmir, this seventeen-day South Asian conflict featured the largest tank battle since 1945 before ending via a Soviet- and U.S.-brokered ceasefire — which conflict?
India–Pakistan war of 1965: Armed conflict. Much of the war was fought by the countries' land forces in Kashmir and along the border between India and Pakistan.

Born in 1936, this British hereditary peer and investment banker was the eldest son of a peer of the same surname, educated at Eton College and Christ Church, Oxford, and left the family bank he'd joined after a 1980 dispute — who was he?
Jacob Rothschild, 4th Baron Rothschild: English peer, investment banker and philanthropist (1936–2024)

The first woman elected as both a judge and district attorney in New York's Westchester County, this television host went on to become the U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia in 2025 — who is she?
Jeanine Pirro: American television host, author and attorney (born 1951)
A former police officer who rose to deputy commissioner, this politician was the sole candidate approved by Beijing in the 2022 election that made him Hong Kong's chief executive — who is he?
John Lee Ka-chiu: Chief Executive of Hong Kong since 2022. After Carrie Lam became chief executive in 2017, Lee was promoted to secretary for security.
This Roman military commander proclaimed himself dictator for life in 44 BC before being dramatically removed from power—by his own senators. Who was he?
Julius Caesar: Roman general and dictator (100–44 BC)
This German Social Democratic politician led the party's youth wing, the Jusos, before serving as SPD General Secretary from 2021 to 2024 — who is he?
Beginning in 1587 with a merchant who settled in Essen, this German dynasty built a steelmaking and arms empire that became the official weapons supplier to Prussia in 1859 — which family?
Krupp family: German dynasty from Essen. The Krupp family is a prominent 400-year-old German dynasty from Essen, noted for its production of steel, artillery, ammunition and other armaments.
After overseeing construction of the Pentagon, this U.S. Army engineer directed the top-secret program that produced the atomic bomb — who is he?

The illegitimate daughter of Pope Alexander VI, this Italian noblewoman was married off three times to advance her family's political fortunes and later became a byword for the femme fatale — who was she?
In the Gospels, Jesus warns that no one can serve God alongside this Aramaic personification of wealth, later depicted in medieval tradition as one of Hell's princes of greed — what is it?
Mammon: Wealth or an entity that promises wealth.

This Baptist minister and civil rights leader championed nonviolent resistance from 1955 until his assassination in 1968, overseeing the Montgomery bus boycott and helping dismantle Jim Crow laws. Who was he?
Martin Luther King Jr.: American minister and civil rights activist (1929–1968)

A composite of earlier Welsh prophet figures named Myrddin and Emrys, this legendary wizard served as advisor to Uther Pendragon in tales popularized by 12th-century writer Geoffrey of Monmouth — who is he?
Merlin: Legendary Welsh wizard. Geoffrey's account presented Merlin as a prophet and royal advisor to Arthur's father, Uther Pendragon.
This ancient Levantine kingdom along the Dead Sea's eastern shore is known from the Mesha Stele, which records its victory over a son of Israel's King Omri — what was it?
Moab: Ancient kingdom East of the Dead Sea. Moab was an ancient Levantine kingdom whose territory is today located in southern Jordan.

Active from 1929 to 1941, this organized crime enforcement squad carried out between 400 and 1,000 contract killings for the National Crime Syndicate before being exposed by a turncoat member nicknamed 'Kid Twist.' What was this group called?
Murder, Inc.: American organized crime groups in the 1930s and 1940s.
A Florentine diplomat of the Italian Renaissance, this man wrote a famous political treatise published only after his death and is often called the father of modern political science — who was he?
Niccolò Machiavelli: Florentine statesman, diplomat, and political theorist (1469–1527)
Serving as Ukraine's Minister of Defence from late 2021 until his dismissal in 2023, this politician previously held several other senior government roles in Kyiv — who is he?
Oleksii Reznikov: Ukrainian lawyer and politician (born 1966)
Assassinated in 1961, this pan-Africanist served as the first prime minister of the newly independent Congo before the Congo Crisis erupted?
Patrice Lumumba: Congolese politician and independence leader (1925–1961)
Known as the 'Bandit Queen,' this Indian outlaw-turned-politician was charged in absentia over a 1981 massacre before later serving as a member of parliament — who is she?
Phoolan Devi: Indian bandit and politician (1963–2001)
He ascended a throne at age two in 1908, then later reigned as a puppet emperor for a wartime Japanese state and was held as a war criminal until 1959 — which last emperor of China is he?
Puyi: Emperor of China (1908–1912) and of Manchukuo (1934–1945)
This Oglala Lakota leader won the war that bears his name, making the Lakota the only nation to defeat the U.S. on American soil — who was he?
Red Cloud: Leader of the Oglala Lakota (1822–1909)
Elected in January 2022 after the sudden death of her predecessor, this Maltese politician became the youngest-ever, and first Maltese, president of a major European institution — who is she?
Roberta Metsola: President of the European Parliament since 2022.

As students in 1930s Paris, this Syrian and Michel Aflaq cooked up a doctrine blending nationalism and socialism, then co-founded the Ba'ath Party — and decades later he was assassinated in Paris. Who is it?
Sparked by a succession crisis after King Frederick VII died heirless, Prussian and Austrian troops crossed into a Danish-controlled duchy in February 1864 — which 19th-century conflict?
Second Schleswig War: War between Denmark, Prussia, and Austria in 1864.

Formed in 2022 after a leadership split within a major Maharashtra party, this faction led by former chief minister Uddhav Thackeray was given a new 'Flaming Torch' symbol by India's Election Commission — which party?
Shiv Sena (UBT): Political party in Maharashtra, India. Shiv Sena (Uddhav Balasaheb Thackeray) (ISO: Śiva Sēnā (Uddhava Bāḷāsāhēba Ṭhākare); lit. 'Army of Shivaji, led by Uddhav Thackeray'; abbr.
Sparked in 1898 by the sinking of the USS Maine in Havana Harbor, this brief conflict handed the U.S. control of Puerto Rico, Guam, and the Philippines — what was it?
Spanish–American War: 1898 conflict between Spain and the United States.
Sparked by Arab Spring protests against Bashar al-Assad in March 2011, this nearly 14-year conflict ended with the regime's fall in December 2024 — what is it?
Syrian civil war: 2011–2024 armed conflict in Syria.

Ruling the Ostrogothic Kingdom of Italy from 493 to 526 and later regent of the Visigoths too, this king received the old Western imperial regalia from Constantinople and was addressed by Italy's aristocracy as princeps. Who was he?
Theodoric the Great: King of Italy from 493 to 526. As ruler of the combined Gothic realms, Theodoric controlled an empire stretching from the Atlantic Ocean to the Adriatic Sea.

Walled off to the east and south by the Carpathians and to the west by the Apuseni Mountains, this historical region sits in central Romania and goes by Erdély in Hungarian and Siebenbürgen in German. What is it?
Transylvania: Historical region in Central Europe. Broader definitions of Transylvania also include the western and northwestern Romanian regions of Crișana and Maramureș, and occasionally Banat.
The last man standing in the Year of the Four Emperors, this Roman founded the Flavian dynasty and was the first emperor to rise from an equestrian family. Who was he?
Vespasian: Roman emperor from AD 69 to 79.

Fought alongside a wider Georgian civil conflict, this early-1990s fight pitted government forces against separatists backed by North Caucasian militants, Cossacks, and the Russian military — which conflict?
War in Abkhazia (1992–1993): Conflict between Georgia and Abkhaz separatists.

A German Army intelligence officer in occupied Warsaw during WWII, this man is credited with saving several Polish Jews, including pianist Władysław Szpilman — his story was dramatized in The Pianist. Who was he?
Wilm Hosenfeld: German army officer (1895–1952) and Righteous among the Nations.

After helping secure the Qing dynasty's abdication, this Chinese general became the Republic's first formal president, only to declare himself emperor in 1915 and abdicate again months later — who was he?
Yuan Shikai: First president of the Republic of China (1859–1916)
Which one below was born first?
John Ray (born 1627) is the earliest of the four. John Ray (29 November 1627 – 17 January 1705) was an English Christian naturalist and one of the earliest English parson-naturalists.
Who among these was born first?
Ma Jun (mechanical engineer) (born 200) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four has been around longest?
C++ (founded 1983) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is the oldest?
Haskell (founded 1990) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below is best known as an astronomer?
Edwin Hubble is an astronomer. Edwin Powell Hubble (November 20, 1889 – September 28, 1953) was an American astronomer.
Which one below is best known as a mathematician?
Archimedes is a mathematician. Archimedes died during the siege of Syracuse, when he was killed by a Roman soldier despite orders that he should not be harmed.
What is the atomic number of Radium?
Radium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ra and atomic number 88.
What is the atomic number of Zinc?
Zinc is a chemical element; it has symbol Zn and atomic number 30.
In what year did Stephen Hawking die?
Stephen Hawking: Hawking was born in Oxford into a family of physicians.
In what year was Theobroma cacao discovered?
Theobroma cacao (cacao tree or cocoa tree) is a small (6–12 m (20–39 ft) tall) evergreen tree in the Malvaceae family.
Mikoyan MiG-31: Russian Aircraft Corporation MiG. The MiG-31 is the fastest known operational combat aircraft, with a top speed around 3,000 km/h (1,600 knots).
Which company manufactures CAC/PAC JF-17 Thunder?
CAC/PAC JF-17 Thunder: Chengdu Aircraft Industry Group. The JF-17 can be used for multiple roles, including interception, ground attack, anti-ship, and aerial reconnaissance.
Who is credited with discovering Triangulum Australe?
Triangulum Australe: Américo Vespucio. Triangulum Australe is a small constellation in the far Southern Celestial Hemisphere.
Who is credited with discovering Ichthyosaurus?
Ichthyosaurus: Mary Anning. It is among the best known ichthyosaur genera, as it is the type genus of the order Ichthyosauria.
Who is credited with discovering Theobroma cacao?
Theobroma cacao: Christopher Columbus. Theobroma cacao (cacao tree or cocoa tree) is a small (6–12 m (20–39 ft) tall) evergreen tree in the Malvaceae family.
Who is credited with discovering Krypton?
Krypton: William Ramsay. Krypton (from Ancient Greek: κρυπτός, romanized: kryptos 'the hidden one') is a chemical element; it has symbol Kr and atomic number 36.

First coined as a term in 1852, this pattern of continued drinking despite its harms affected an estimated 283 million people worldwide as of 2016, according to the World Health Organization — name the condition?
Alcoholism is the continued drinking of alcohol despite the problems it causes.
This order of ray-finned fish is named for a modified fin ray that dangles like bait to lure in prey, much like a human with a fishing rod — what are they called?

Anglerfish are ray-finned fish in the order Lophiiformes. The majority are bottom-dwellers, being demersal fish, while the aberrant deep-sea anglerfish are pelagic, (mostly) living high in the water column.

This English science fiction writer, futurist, and undersea explorer received the 1961 Kalinga Prize, a UNESCO award for popularizing science, across a career spanning novels, essays, and television hosting — who is he?
Arthur C. Clarke (16 December 1917 - 19 March 2008) was an English science fiction writer, science writer, futurist, inventor, undersea explorer, and television series host.
Coming on over about 48 hours, this temporary one-sided facial paralysis of unknown cause can droop an eyebrow, alter taste, and make sounds painfully loud — what is it?
Bell's palsy is a type of facial paralysis that results in a temporary inability to control the facial muscles on the affected side of the face.
Element 107, a synthetic transactinide whose most stable known isotope lasts barely 2.4 minutes, takes its name from a famous Danish physicist — what is it?
Bohrium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Bh and atomic number 107.
Unlike ordinary weight loss from undereating, this illness-linked syndrome strips away muscle mass in ways good nutrition can't fully undo — what condition is it?
Cachexia is a syndrome that occurs in people with certain illnesses, causing muscle loss that cannot be fully reversed with improved nutrition.

Derived from the amino acid tyrosine and fifty percent bound to plasma proteins in your bloodstream, what class of neurotransmitter has a benzene ring topped with two hydroxyl groups plus a side-chain amine?

Catecholamine (abbreviated CA), most typically a 3,4-dihydroxyphenethylamine, is a monoamine neurotransmitter, an organic compound that has a catechol (benzene with two hydroxyl side groups next to each other) and a side-chain amine.
Grown for blue-flowered roadside roots that become a coffee substitute, or for bitter salad leaves like escarole and radicchio, which plant genus covers both chicory and endive?
Cichorium is a genus of plants in the tribe Cichorieae within the family Asteraceae.
This common bowel condition causes hard, dry stools passed fewer than three times a week, sometimes leading to hemorrhoids or fissures — what is it?
Constipation is a bowel dysfunction that makes bowel movements infrequent or hard to pass.
This Canadian-born entrepreneur co-founded a company later acquired by MSC Software in 1998, then went on to co-found and lead a massively popular online gaming and creation platform — who is he?
David Baszucki (buh-; born January 20, 1963) is a Canadian-born American entrepreneur, engineer, and software developer.
First proposed as a model organism in 1901, this tiny insect species has become biology's workhorse for genetics research, and it's the one buzzing around your rotting fruit bowl. Name the species?
Drosophila melanogaster is a species of fly (an insect of the order Diptera) in the family Drosophilidae.
Practitioners of this zoological discipline have identified more than 1.3 million species within a single group of arthropods — what is it called?
Entomology (ntomon), meaning "insect", and (lgos), meaning "study", is the branch of zoology that focuses on insects.

This synthetic opioid is 50 to 100 times more potent than morphine and is now notorious in emergency medicine. Initially developed as a pain medication for cancer patients and post-surgical recovery, it works by activating opioid receptors — what is this drug?
Fentanyl is a highly potent synthetic opioid of the piperidine family, used primarily as pain medication.

Derived from a Greek word meaning 'milky,' this term names any gravity-bound system of stars, gas, dust, and dark matter, ranging from tiny dwarfs to supergiants with a hundred trillion stars. What is it?
Galaxy is a system of stars, stellar remnants, interstellar gas, dust, and dark matter bound together by gravity.
This large, semi-bitter citrus fruit originated in Barbados as an accidental 18th-century hybrid of the sweet orange and the pomelo, and has also been called the 'forbidden fruit.' What is it?
Grapefruit (Citrus paradisi) is a subtropical citrus tree known for its relatively large, sour to semi-sweet, somewhat bitter fruit.

Known as 'The Last Universalist' for mastering nearly every branch of his field, this French mathematician and physicist founded modern chaos theory through his study of the three-body problem — who is he?
Henri Poincaré (29 April 1854 - 17 July 1912) was a French mathematician, theoretical physicist, engineer, and philosopher of science.
A body-temperature emergency defined as a reading above 104°F, this condition kills roughly half a million people annually and is most commonly triggered by heat stroke — what is it called?
Hyperthermia is a condition in which an individual's body temperature is elevated beyond normal due to failed thermoregulation.

From deep-sea gribbles to the woodlice under your garden stones, members of this crustacean order share seven pairs of jointed limbs and brood their young in a pouch called a marsupium — what is the order?
Isopoda is an order of crustaceans. The order is divided into eleven suborders.

After leaving the company where he led industrial design for decades, this British-American designer founded the creative collective LoveFrom, which now works with Ferrari, Airbnb, and OpenAI. Who is he?
Jony Ive (born 27 February 1967) is a British-American designer.
This genus of deciduous conifers, unusual for shedding its needles each year, dominates the boreal forests of Siberia and Canada, making it the most abundant tree genus on Earth — what is it called?
Larch are deciduous conifers in the genus Larix, of the family Pinaceae.
Only about 35 atoms of this synthetic element (symbol Lv, number 116) had ever been made as of 2020 — named for a California national laboratory. Which element is it?
Livermorium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Lv and atomic number 116.
Sometimes nicknamed 'sea cows,' these large, fully aquatic herbivorous marine mammals can grow up to 13 feet long and include Amazonian, West Indian, and West African species — what are they called?
Manatee (family Trichechidae, genus Trichechus) are large, fully aquatic, mostly herbivorous marine mammals sometimes known as sea cows.
Its three main jobs are converting food into usable energy, building macromolecules like proteins and lipids, and excreting waste — the chemistry that keeps every living thing alive. What is it?
Metabolism (from) refers to the set of life-sustaining chemical reactions that occur within living organisms.
Named for the river near which its type fossil was found by a Dutch chalk quarry in the 18th century, this genus of marine reptile lived until the end of the Cretaceous — what is it?
Mosasaurus ("lizard of the Meuse River") is the type genus (defining example) of the Mosasauridae, an extinct group of aquatic squamate reptiles.
Named for a pioneering physicist's work on classical mechanics, this SI unit of force equals the push needed to accelerate one kilogram at one metre per second squared — name the unit?
Newton (unit) (symbol: N) is the unit of force in the International System of Units (SI).

These pouched mammals originated in South America and crossed into the north during the Great American Interchange; one species is so common in the U.S. that people just call it a 'possum.' What is it?
Opossum are members of the marsupial order Didelphimorphia endemic to the Americas.
This New York Times columnist of 24 years was the sole winner of the 2008 Nobel in economics for explaining the patterns of international trade and where economic activity clusters. Who is he?
Paul Krugman (born February 28, 1953) is an American economist who is the Distinguished Professor of Economics at the Graduate Center of the City University of New York.
Odorless when pure but reeking of rotting fish in technical grade, this colorless PH3 gas can burst into a luminous flame on contact with air — what highly toxic compound is it?
Phosphine (IUPAC name: phosphane) is a colorless, flammable, highly toxic compound with the chemical formula PH3, classed as a pnictogen hydride.
Though it looks like a small dolphin, this cetacean is actually more closely related to narwhals and belugas, and can be told apart by its flattened, spade-shaped teeth — what animal is it?
Porpoise are small dolphin-like cetaceans classified under the family Phocoenidae.
Its blossoms are a beloved symbol of early spring throughout East Asia, and its crunchy fruit is marketed globally as the Asian or nashi pear - which tree species?
Pyrus pyrifolia is a species of pear tree native to southern China and northern Indochina that has been introduced to Korea, Japan and other parts of the world.

A brilliant English anatomist who coined the word 'Dinosauria,' meaning roughly 'terrible reptile,' he accepted that evolution happened but was an outspoken critic of Darwin's account of it. Who was he?
Richard Owen (20 July 1804 - 18 December 1892) was an English biologist, comparative anatomist and palaeontologist.
Marked by hearing voices, disorganized thinking, and flat affect, this condition is diagnosed by observed behavior rather than any objective test — what is it?
Schizophrenia is a mental disorder characterized variously by hallucinations (typically, hearing voices), delusions, disorganized thinking or behavior, and flat or inappropriate affect.
Long, thin and transparent, this hydrozoan drifts through the ocean as a colony of specialized zooids that together handle feeding, floating and jet propulsion — what marine organism is this?
Siphonophore (from Ancient Greek (siphn), meaning "tube" and - (-phros), meaning "bearing") are cnidarian animals of the hydrozoan order Siphonophorae.

Named in 1880 from Greek words meaning 'bunch of grapes' and 'kernel,' this genus of spherical, Gram-positive bacteria grows in grape-like clusters and can survive with or without oxygen — what's the genus called?
Staphylococcus (staphul), meaning "bunch of grapes", and (kkkos), meaning "kernel" or "Kermes", is a genus of Gram-positive bacteria in the family Staphylococcaceae from the order Bacillales.
Though some scientists place it in its own genus, Acrocodia, the Malayan species is usually still classified within this genus of tapir — name this genus?
Tapirus is a genus of tapir which contains the living tapir species.
This intensely itchy, contagious fungal skin infection produces a red, scaly rash with a curved border across the groin and buttocks, mostly in men — what is it?

Tinea cruris (TC), also known as jock itch, is a common type of contagious, superficial fungal infection of the groin and buttocks region, which occurs predominantly but not exclusively in men and in hot-humid climates.
This bodily fluid, produced by the kidneys to flush out urea and other waste, can also serve a second life as a nitrogen-rich fertilizer for soil — what is it?
Urine is the fluid excreted by the kidneys of vertebrates to clear the bloodstream of excess water and metabolic by-products including urea, uric acid, and creatinine.
Native to Eastern and Southern Africa, this large antelope genus includes two species — one black, one blue — whose lineages diverged roughly a million years ago — what animal is it?
Wildebeest (VIL-), also called gnu (NOO or, NEW), are antelopes of the genus Connochaetes and native to Eastern and Southern Africa.

This symptom can stem from something as mild as gastroenteritis or as serious as a ruptured aortic aneurysm or ectopic pregnancy, yet its exact cause goes unexplained in about a third of cases — what symptom is this?
Native to China and Taiwan, this fast-growing deciduous tree can reach 15 meters in 25 years and has become notorious in North America as a host plant for the invasive spotted lanternfly. What is it?
Ailanthus altissima: Deciduous tree in the quassia family.
This military pilot became his country's first astronaut when he flew to the International Space Station aboard a 2024 mission — who is he?
Alper Gezeravcı: Turkish fighter pilot and astronaut (born 1979)
Commonly called windflowers, which genus of the buttercup family is native to every continent except Australia, New Zealand, and Antarctica?
Anemone: Genus of flowering plants in the family Ranunculaceae.
Also nicknamed the cross spider or diadem spider for the white markings on its back, this orb-weaver is native to Europe but was introduced to North America — what species is it?

Araneus diadematus: Species of spider. The spider species Araneus diadematus is commonly called the European garden spider, cross orbweaver, diadem spider, orangie, cross spider, and crowned orb weaver.
The third-largest fish in its family, behind Siberian taimen and Pacific Chinook, this species is unusual for surviving spawning and returning to sea to breed again — which fish?
Atlantic salmon: Species of fish. The Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar) is a species of ray-finned fish in the family Salmonidae.
Named for the physicist who shared a 1903 Nobel Prize with Pierre and Marie Curie, this SI unit measures one radioactive decay event per second — which unit?
Becquerel: SI derived unit of radioactivity.
Despite its name, only the soles of this tawny, spotted feline's paws are actually dark — and at just 35 to 52 centimetres long, it ranks as Africa's smallest wild feline species — what animal is it?
Black-footed cat: Small wild cat native to Southern Africa.
Also known as warble flies or gadflies, the larvae of which insect family live as internal parasites in mammal flesh or gut, with one species routinely infesting humans?
Botfly: Parasitic insect. Dermatobia hominis is the only species of botfly known to parasitize humans routinely, though other species of flies cause myiasis in humans.
He piloted the Lunar Module Eagle in 1969 to become the second person to walk on the Moon, and after Jim Lovell's death in 2025 became the oldest living astronaut — who is he?
Tetravalent and able to form four covalent bonds, this element known since antiquity ranks as the fourth most abundant in the universe by mass — which one is it?
Carbon: Chemical element with atomic number 6 (C)

Greek for "head-feet," fishers nickname these inkfish for their ink-squirting trick; their arms are muscular hydrostats modified from the primitive molluscan foot. Which marine class includes the octopus, squid, and nautilus?
Cephalopod: Class of mollusks. The study of cephalopods is a branch of malacology known as teuthology.
Made in the skin after sun exposure and also known as vitamin D3, this compound is converted by the liver and kidneys into forms that help the body absorb calcium. What is it?

Cholecalciferol: Vitamin D3, a chemical compound. Cholecalciferol, also known as vitamin D3, colecalciferol or calciol, is a skin-made vitamin D that is found in certain foods and used as a dietary supplement.
This scale insect that feeds on prickly pear cacti produces carminic acid, the basis of the red dye carmine used in lipstick and food coloring — what is it?
Cochineal: Species of insect producing the crimson dye carmine.
Known historically as blue vitriol, this bright blue crystalline compound with the formula CuSO4 forms an octahedral complex when dissolved in water — what compound?
Copper(II) sulfate: Chemical compound. It forms hydrates CuSO4·nH2O, where n can range from 1 to 7.
Named for the ancient Greek word for a ship's helmsman, this transdisciplinary field studies feedback loops and circular causal processes across engineering, biology, and social systems — what is it?

Cybernetics: Study of circular causal processes. Cybernetics' transdisciplinary character means that it intersects with a number of other fields, resulting in a wide influence and diverse interpretations.
This autoimmune disease attacks both the skin and skeletal muscles, causing a rash alongside worsening weakness, and is often linked to distinct myositis-specific autoantibodies — which condition?
Dermatomyositis: Autoimmune disease of skin and muscle. Dermatomyositis (DM) is a group of sytemic autoimmune inflammatory diseases primarily affecting the skin and skeletal muscles.

Originally developed to compete for a USAF aerial-tanker contract it lost to Boeing's Stratotanker, this four-engined jetliner instead entered airline service with Delta in 1959 — what aircraft was it?
Douglas DC-8: American four-engined jet airliner family.
This membrane-bound series of protein complexes shuttles electrons through redox reactions, building a proton gradient that ultimately powers the synthesis of ATP — what's it called?
Electron transport chain: Energy-producing metabolic pathway.
Named from the Greek for 'red skin,' this bacterial infection produces a raised, sharply defined, bright-red rash typically on the face or legs — what's the condition?
Erysipelas: Human disease from a bacterial infection of the skin.
Also nicknamed the 'baum' or 'sweet' variety, this mustelid species ranges across much of the continent into Asia Minor, the Caucasus, and parts of Iran, Iraq, and Syria. What animal is it?
European pine marten: Species of mammal in the mustelid family.

This branch of Islamic scholarship interprets the Quran and sunnah through jurist reasoning, producing fatwas — while sharia itself is seen as unchanging, this human field is considered fallible. What is it called?
Fiqh: Islamic jurisprudence. Thus, whereas sharia is considered immutable and infallible by Muslims, fiqh is considered fallible and changeable.
This cold-weather injury turns skin white or waxy-blue after tissue actually freezes, often preceded by a tingling, numb warning stage called frostnip — what is it?
Frostbite: Effect of low temperature on skin and other tissues.

Predicted by Mendeleev in 1869 under the placeholder name 'ekasilicon' and discovered in 1886 by Clemens Winkler, this metalloid element was named for its discoverer's home country — what element is it?
Germanium: Chemical element with atomic number 32 (Ge)
One of China's 'Four Great Domestic Fish,' this herbivorous freshwater species was later introduced to Europe and the US to control aquatic weeds — which fish?
Grass carp: Species of fish. This Asian carp is the only species of the genus Ctenopharyngodon.
The son of a famous physicist and his first wife, this Swiss-American engineer taught hydraulic engineering at Berkeley and became renowned for research on sediment transport — who is he?

Hans Albert Einstein: Swiss-American engineer and educator. Hans Albert Einstein (May 14, 1904 – July 26, 1973) was a Swiss-American engineer, the second child and first son of physicists Albert Einstein and Mileva Marić.
In this condition, part of the stomach slips upward through the diaphragm into the chest, often triggering acid reflux, heartburn, or trouble swallowing — what is it?
Hiatal hernia: Entrance of abdominal organs into the middle chest through the diaphragm.
Also called prussic acid, this toxic, flammable liquid with the formula HCN boils just above room temperature and serves as an industrial precursor to plastics and mining chemicals — what is it?
Traditionally drawn from the leaves of Indigofera plants and now mostly made synthetically, this blue compound is the color most associated with denim and blue jeans — what is it?
Indigo dye: Chemical compound, food additive and dye.
Before he proposed that the Earth behaves like one self-regulating living system, this English independent scientist built the detector that first revealed CFCs lurking in our atmosphere. Who was he?

An Alberta-born clinical psychologist and University of Toronto professor, he drew huge attention in the late 2010s for his cultural and political views — self-identifying as a classical liberal. Who is he?
Also called German turnip despite not being related to true turnips, this stout cabbage cultivar can be eaten raw or cooked, stem and leaves alike — what vegetable?
Kohlrabi: Biennial cultivar of wild cabbage.
Also known as Peruvian ginseng, this Andean root crop is grown at high altitude in Peru and Bolivia and exported worldwide as a dietary powder — what plant is it?
Lepidium meyenii: Plant species native to South America.
Developed under Kelly Johnson's Skunk Works team after the discovery of Germany's Me 262, this aircraft became the first jet fighter flown operationally by U.S. forces in World War II — which jet?
Lockheed P-80 Shooting Star: First jet aircraft in U.S. operational service.
Best known in its heptahydrate form as Epsom salt, this white crystalline compound (MgSO4) is also used in agriculture to fix soils deficient in an essential plant nutrient — what compound is it?
Magnesium sulfate: Chemical compound with formula MgSO4.
Born in Erfurt in 1864, this German jurist-turned-scholar became one of the founding figures of sociology before a breakdown following his father's death halted his teaching — who was he?
Max Weber: German sociologist, jurist, and political economist (1864–1920)
Originally known as amethopterin, this chemotherapy drug also treats autoimmune conditions like rheumatoid arthritis and psoriasis, and can end ectopic pregnancies — what is it?
Sold under the brand name Provigil, this first-line narcolepsy treatment boosts dopamine without the euphoria or addiction risk of classic stimulants like amphetamine — what is it?
Lacking a cell wall entirely, this genus of bacteria is naturally resistant to beta-lactam antibiotics that target cell-wall synthesis — which genus?
Mycoplasma: Genus of bacteria. Mycoplasma is a genus of bacteria that, like the other members of the class Mollicutes, lack a cell wall (peptidoglycan) around their cell membrane.

Published in the Principia Mathematica, this principle holds that every particle in the cosmos attracts every other with a pull proportional to their masses and inversely proportional to the squared distance between them — which principle is it?
Newton's law of universal gravitation: Classical statement of gravity as force.
First described by Linnaeus in 1758, this medium-sized spotted wild cat hunts armadillos and opossums at twilight across a range from the southwestern US to South America — what cat is it?
Ocelot: Species of wild cat. It is native to the southwestern United States, Mexico, Central and South America, and the Caribbean islands of Trinidad and Margarita.

Most members of this order of over 200 species are solitary night hunters with broad heads, binocular vision, and feathers tuned for silent flight — though oddballs like the burrowing kind break the mold. What are they?
Owl: Birds from the order Strigiformes.
Nicknamed the empress tree for its fast growth and showy foxglove-like blooms, which East Asian hardwood has become an invasive species across the Eastern US?
Paulownia tomentosa: Species of deciduous tree classified in its own family.

Combining textual criticism, literary criticism, history, and linguistics, this scholarly field traces its classical roots to the libraries of Pergamum and Alexandria in the 4th century BC — what is it?
Philology: Study of language in historical sources.
Commonly called frangipani, this fragrant flowering shrub native to Mexico and the Caribbean is now a beloved ornamental in Hawaii and desert climates of Arabia — what genus is it?
Plumeria: Genus of flowering plants endemic to the Americas.
Sold under the brand name Phenergan, this first-generation antihistamine treats allergies and nausea but has also seen recreational misuse alongside codeine — which drug?
Promethazine: Sedating antihistamine. Promethazine is taken by mouth (oral), as a rectal suppository, or by injection into a muscle (IM).
Once one of America's leading rocket experts with an MIT aeronautics degree, he was deported to China in 1955 and went on to father that nation's space program — which aerospace engineer?

Nicknamed the 'Jug,' this WWII American fighter-bomber carried eight .50-caliber machine guns and weighed up to eight tons fully loaded, making it one of the heaviest fighters of the war — which aircraft?

Republic P-47 Thunderbolt: Family of fighter aircraft. The Republic P-47 Thunderbolt (nicknamed the "Jug") is a World War II-era fighter aircraft produced by the American company Republic Aviation from 1941 through 1945.
Also known as sixth disease, this childhood viral infection typically strikes before age three with a sudden fever followed by a pink rash lasting under three days — what's the condition called?
Roseola: Human disease caused by human herpesviruses.

Sometimes nicknamed the "seven-year itch," this contagious infestation by a tiny burrowing mite spreads fastest in crowded places and announces itself with fierce itching and a pimple-like rash — what is it?
Nicknamed the 'Human Computer' for her lightning mental arithmetic, this Indian writer also authored one of the earliest studies of homosexuality in India, back in 1977 — who is she?
Shakuntala Devi: Indian writer and mental calculator (1929–2013)

Historically mined in vast deposits and nicknamed 'Chile saltpeter,' this white, water-soluble alkali metal compound is used in fertilizers, fireworks, meat preservation, and solid rocket fuel. What is it?
Sodium nitrate: Chemical compound. The mineral form is also known as nitratine, nitratite or soda niter.
Derived from the Greek word for 'narrow,' this medical term describes the abnormal tightening of a blood vessel or other tubular structure — what is it?
Stenosis: Medical condition. Stenosis (from Ancient Greek στενός (stenós) 'narrow') is the abnormal narrowing of a blood vessel or other tubular organ or structure such as foramina and canals.
Defined by a single skull opening behind each eye socket that anchors larger jaw muscles, this major branch of the amniote family tree includes all mammals and their extinct kin — which clade?
Synapsida: Clade of tetrapods. Synapsida is a diverse group of tetrapod vertebrates that includes all mammals and their extinct relatives.
Also sold under the name dronabinol, this principal psychoactive compound in cannabis is prescribed to relieve chemotherapy-induced nausea and HIV/AIDS-related appetite loss — what is it?
Tetrahydrocannabinol: Psychoactive component of cannabis. It is the principal psychoactive constituent of Cannabis and one of at least 113 total cannabinoids identified on the plant.
Sitting between cells and organs in the body's organization, this assembly of similar cells and their extracellular matrix takes its English name from a French word meaning 'to weave' — what is it?
Tissue (biology): Group of similar cells performing a specific function.
Roughly three times stiffer than steel and nearly as hard as diamond, this gray powder is sintered into cutting tools, armor-piercing bullets, and jewelry — what compound is it?
Tungsten carbide: Hard, dense and stiff chemical compound.
Unlike arteries, most of these thin-walled blood vessels carry deoxygenated blood back toward the heart — what are they?
Vein: Blood vessels that carry blood towards the heart.
A slow-moving filter-feeder and the largest known fish alive — the biggest reliably recorded stretched nearly 19 metres — this is the only living member of its family. What is it?
Whale shark: Largest living species of fish. The whale shark (Rhincodon typus) is a slow-moving, filter-feeding carpet shark and the largest known extant fish species.

Distinguished by a fatty hump on its shoulders and a large dewlap, this heat-tolerant type of domestic cattle originated in South Asia and holds religious significance in parts of the world — what is it?
Zebu: South Asian domestic cattle. The zebu (Bos indicus), also known as indicine cattle and humped cattle, is a species or subspecies of domestic cattle originating in South Asia.

The symbol for barium is Ba. Barium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ba and atomic number 56.
